sources.entry: vod2pod-rss ⚠ - Convert YouTube and Twitch channels to podcasts, no storage required. Transcodes VoDs to MP3 192k on the fly, generates an RSS feed to use in podcast clients. MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: vod2pod-rss turns YouTube and Twitch channels (and standard RSS feeds) into audio podcast feeds, transcoding VoDs to MP3 on the fly without storing them on the server.
summary.what_it_does: The app converts a YouTube or Twitch channel into a podcast RSS feed that can be added to a podcast client. It includes a web UI where you paste a channel URL and copy the generated feed link. VoDs are not downloaded to the server; audio is transcoded to MP3 (192k by default, configurable via MP3_BITRATE) on the fly as it is played. It can also pass through standard RSS/Atom podcast feeds, optionally at a lower bitrate. Optional YouTube and Twitch API keys raise the YouTube item limit above 15 and add a channel avatar and Twitch access. Transcoding can be disabled with TRANSCODE=false if only feeds are needed. Domains allowed for conversion are restricted by VALID_URL_DOMAINS, and cache lifetime is set by CACHE_TTL.
use_cases: listen to YouTube channels as podcasts
turn Twitch VODs into audio episodes
generate a podcast feed for a video channel
save mobile data by using low-bitrate audio feeds
self-host a podcast feed converter without disk storage
run a media feed service on a Raspberry Pi
how_to_run: edit docker-compose.yml to set ports and optional API keys (YT_API_KEY, TWITCH_SECRET, TWITCH_CLIENT_ID)
open the web UI on the hosted port, paste a channel URL, and copy the generated RSS link into a podcast client
notable: No media storage: VoDs are transcoded on the fly rather than downloaded to the server
Precompiled Docker images for arm64, amd64 and armv7, including Raspberry Pi
Beta image tag tracks latest yt-dlp releases for faster fixes
Optional YouTube extra yt-dlp arguments, such as a proxy or custom user-agent
Also accepts standard RSS/Atom podcast feeds for lower-bitrate versions
caveats: Without a YouTube API key, YouTube feeds are limited to 15 items and have no channel avatar
Twitch support requires your own Twitch client ID and secret for API access
Listed on awesome-selfhosted with a warning marker; the README does not state a maintenance status
